newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Res to buy parent's stake in HKCB.
newsitem.headline: China Res to buy parent's stake in HKCB.

text.p: Red chip conglomerate China Resources Enterprise Ltd is taking a major step into the banking and finance industry with the purchase of a stake in The Hongkong Chinese Bank Ltd, its chairman said on Wednesday.
The company is buying the stake in the bank, and also a concrete manufacturer, from its parent China Resources (Holdings) Ltd.

"We are paying HK$2 billion for the stake (in the bank), HK$1 billion in cash and the remaining in new shares to be issued to the parent company," said chairman Zhu Youlan at a news conference after the company's annual general meeting.
At present, parent China Resources (Holdings) Ltd has 1.10 percent of The HKCB Bank Holding Co Ltd, whose main asset is its 50 percent stake in The Hongkong Chinese Bank Ltd.
China Resources (Holdings) also directly holds a 50 percent stake in The Hongkong Chinese Bank Ltd. Indonesia-linked Lippo Ltd holds 59.33 percent of HKCB Bank Holding.
"The purchase price valued the bank at 10.5 times earnings," chairman Zhu said.
The price and number of new China Resources Enterprises shares to be issued had not yet been fixed, Zhu said.

A further step would be an exchange of shares between China Resources Enterprises and Lippo which would result in both parties holding 37.5 percent of the listed share capital of HKCB Holding, the chairman said, but gave no other details.
"We are planning to increase the capital base of the bank, investing about another HK$2 billion," said the chairman.
The company has also proposed changing the name of the holding company to CRE Finance Ltd (from The HKCB Bank Holdings Ltd) and changing the bank's name to CRE Bank Ltd.
Trading in shares of HKCB Bank Holdings were suspended on June 6 at HK$6.80.
China Resources Enterprises will also acquire an 80 percent stake in Redland Concrete Ltd from its parent company for HK$700 million in cash, the chairman said.
The company is one of three largest concrete companies in Hong Kong.
"The acquisition price gives a price earnings ratio 7.3 times earnings," said Zhu. "We believe this is a fair price."
The parent company will retain a 20 percent holding in the cement company.

Commenting on the outlook for China Resources Enterprises, the chairman said the main source of earnings in 1997 would be property but other divisions, such as finance and brewery operations, would also see earnings growth.
Trading in shares of China Resources Enterprises was suspended on June 17 at HK$27.70.
